jobs.title: Data Engineer, Deal Intelligence & Automation, AWS GDSP
jobs.description: The Global Deal Strategy and Programs (GDSP) organization is seeking a Data Engineer to own the data infrastructure that unlocks deal intelligence and automation capabilities across the organization. The role is responsible for designing, building, and maintaining the pipelines, data models, and platforms that enable deal teams to access precise, reliable insights from broad data sets (deal telemetry, pricing models, customer usage, pipeline signals) at scale, with speed and accuracy that hold as volume grows. These data products serve deal strategists, pricing leaders, and senior executives who depend on them to structure, evaluate, and negotiate transformative contracts with AWS's most strategic customers. Quality, freshness, and accuracy of data outputs have direct, measurable impact on deal velocity, pricing quality, and revenue outcomes. This is a high-visibility role. The data engineer partners closely with product management to translate analytical requirements into scalable data solutions, and with engineering teams to ensure pipelines integrate cleanly across GDSP's tooling ecosystem. The role will leverage generative AI and AWS services to raise the bar on how GDSP consumes and acts on data. Key job responsibilities - Build and maintain backend data infrastructure for analytical and visualization platforms, ensuring data is clean, fresh, and optimized for downstream consumption - Translate business problem statements into technical data requirements, partnering with product management and stakeholders to define what data products to build - Automate and optimize reporting processes to enable self-service analytics at scale, reducing manual effort and improving speed to insight - Develop measurement frameworks and metrics that quantify deal execution performance and operational health - Ensure data quality through monitoring, validation, auditing, and documentation of pipelines and data sources - Leverage AWS services and generative AI to build next-generation data solutions that improve efficiency and unlock new analytical capabilities About the team The team builds products that power how GDSP operates. Reporting and tooling that are held to the highest standards of clarity, reliability, and scalability. Diverse Experiences AWS values diverse experiences. jobs.title: Software Development Engineer
jobs.description: The Device Ad Products team is hiring Software Development Engineers to help scale and evolve our ad platform for Amazon-owned devices like Fire Tablets, Alexa Tablets, and Echo Show. We’re a lean team with startup energy, backed by Amazon’s infrastructure and resources—giving you the freedom to move fast and the support to build at scale. What You’ll Do You’ll be part of the core engineering team responsible for the systems that power ad delivery, performance optimization, and reporting across devices. These systems process hundreds of millions of events per day, and your work will directly impact latency, data quality, and platform reliability. You’ll design, build, and operate services that: * Optimize ad delivery in real time using data-driven logic (and increasingly, ML/AI models). * Scale backend pipelines to handle high-throughput event ingestion and processing. * Provide accurate and low-latency reporting to advertisers. * Support experimentation and measurement at scale. There are opportunities to work on systems for real-time bidding, targeting, and ad ranking—especially as we explore smarter optimizations for ad placement on-device. Why This Role * Tangible Impact: Your work affects ad experience and monetization across Amazon devices. * Scalable Challenges: Work on high-volume systems where performance and reliability are critical. * Tech Stack Variety: Exposure to AWS services, stream processing frameworks, and multiple programming languages (Java, Kotlin, Python, etc.). * AI Opportunity: Help shape how we apply machine learning and AI to improve targeting, delivery, and measurement. This isn’t a team that throws work over the wall. You’ll be involved from design to deployment—and have a voice in what we build next. If you’re pragmatic, data-driven, and energized by complex distributed systems—and you're curious about how AI can be embedded into production software—we’d love to talk. - 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience - 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience - 1+ years of software development engineer or related occupational experience - 1+ years of designing and developing large-scale, multi-tiered, multi-threaded, embedded or distributed software applications, tools, systems, and services using: C#, C++, Java, or Perl experience - 1+ years of Object Oriented Design experience - Bachelor's degree or foreign equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field - Experience programming with at least one software programming language - 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience - Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status. jobs.title: Software Engineer - AI Tooling
jobs.description: The Development Platform organization at IMC Trading is focused on accelerating tech team workflows by providing self-service tools, services, documentation, and support. We design, build, and maintain the platforms that IMC's software development lifecycle depends on, establishing a consistent technical foundation across regions and empowering teams to innovate efficiently. IMC is embedding agentic AI directly into the developer workflow for our production-critical systems. The Development Platform team operates the infrastructure that makes this possible: the environments where AI agents run, the integrations that connect them to our systems, and the safety and security controls that keep them reliable and auditable. We are seeking a Software Engineer based in Chicago to build the software behind IMC’s AI-powered engineering workflows. Your work will span agent harnesses, developer workspaces, context delivery, and tooling that connects AI agents to internal services. This is a highly collaborative role with substantial ownership. You will engage directly with engineers to understand their needs, connect those needs to the team’s broader priorities, and turn open-ended problems into practical solutions. You will help define what we build and carry it through design, implementation, delivery, and ongoing improvement. You will bring strong software engineering fundamentals and an eagerness to learn. Prior experience building AI tooling is welcome but not required Your Core Responsibilities: Partner directly with engineering teams to understand their workflows, clarify needs, and shape solutions aligned with the team’s broader priorities. Own software projects from problem definition and technical design through implementation, rollout, and ongoing improvement. Develop and extend the agent harnesses and workspace capabilities that bring AI coding tools into IMC's engineering workflows, so engineers get a consistent, high-quality experience wherever they work Improve how agent workflows access relevant context from internal systems, working with stakeholders to define and evolve these capabilities. Develop shared tooling to make MCP servers easier to build and maintain, including standardized authentication patterns, reusable components, and project templates. Contribute to in-house agents for IMC-specific workflows, and to the evaluation and benchmarking tooling to measure quality Embed security, reliability, and observability into the software and integrations you build. Collaborate with global Development Platform colleagues to support adoption, gather feedback, and improve the developer experience. Your Skills & Experience: 3+ years of work experience in a relevant role. Bachelor’s degree in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or equivalent. Strong programming experience in a high-level language; Python or Java preferred. Experience building developer-facing tools, APIs, or production systems. Understanding of security principles and best practices, including authentication and authorization patterns and secrets management. Familiarity with containerization technologies such as Docker and Kubernetes. Curiosity and eagerness to learn about AI/LLM application patterns, even if you haven’t worked closely with them yet; exposure to agentic AI tools and workflows, such as coding agents or MCP servers, is a plus. Strong communication skills and the ability to work directly with stakeholders to understand their needs and connect them to broader team priorities. Ability to take ownership of open-ended problems, shape solutions, and carry them through delivery in a fast, collaborative environment. The Base Salary range for the role is included below. Base salary is only one component of total compensation; all full-time, permanent positions are eligible for a discretionary bonus and benefits, including paid leave and insurance. Please visit Benefits - US | IMC Trading for more comprehensive information. Salary Range $175,000 — $225,000 USD About Us IMC is a research-driven trading firm where quantitative modeling, machine learning, and engineering shape how modern markets are traded. A stabilizing force in markets since 1989, we provide liquidity across trading venues, delivering the best outcome in value and risk management to investors. Using our own technology and capital, we build proprietary systems and algorithms that operate across global markets. Our researchers, traders, and engineers work as a collective, combining rapid experimentation, advanced infrastructure, and real-time feedback to turn insight into execution and execution into advantage.

jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, DynamoDB
jobs.description: Want to help shape the future of one of the largest NoSQL database services on the planet? The Amazon DynamoDB team is looking for deeply technical, team-first-mentality full stack software engineers who are willing to commit themselves to our goal to grow the business 10 times over the next 2 years. DynamoDB is a key-value database that delivers single-digit-millisecond performance at any scale. As a fast-growing service at the core of the AWS Cloud, our business and engineering decisions have widespread impact across AWS, Amazon, and beyond. Many of the world's fastest growing businesses, such as Lyft, Airbnb, and Redfin, as well as enterprises, such as Samsung, Toyota, and Capital One, depend on the scale and performance of DynamoDB to support their mission-critical workloads. DynamoDB engineers are constantly challenged to think of unique and innovative solutions. The quality bar is high. As an engineer here, you will work on the hardest engineering problems in distributed systems at a massive scale and on multiple dimensions. You will exercise your intellectual curiosity, work with motivated teams of sharp individuals, and get insightful guidance from senior and principal engineers. You will be responsible to maintain a high bar in terms of execution, operational readiness, code and design quality. You will serve as a mentor for junior engineers and help them grow. You are comfortable working with other seasoned DynamoDB engineers and hold your ground during design and customer experience reviews. This is a hands-on position where you will own everything from end to end: design, design reviews, implementation, code reviews, iterative feature launches, operations, mentoring, driving continuous improvement, and more. Key job responsibilities Our engineers collaborate across diverse teams, projects, and environments to have a firsthand impact on our global customer base. You’ll bring a passion for innovation, data, search, analytics, and distributed systems. You’ll also: - Solve challenging technical problems, often ones not solved before, at every layer of the stack. - Design, implement, test, deploy and maintain innovative software solutions. - Build high-quality, secure, performant, highly available, always-on products. - Automate and improve repetitive operational processes. - Deep dive and continuously improve performance to deliver superior customer experience. - Scale distributed systems with optimal balance between performance and cost. A day in the life As you design and code solutions to help our team drive efficiencies in software architecture, you’ll create metrics, implement automation and other improvements, and resolve the root cause of software defects. You’ll also: - Build high-impact solutions to deliver to our large customer base. - Participate in design discussions, code review, and communicate with internal and external stakeholders. - Work cross-functionally to help drive business decisions with your technical input. - Work in a startup-like development environment, where you’re always working on the most important stuff. We have a broad mix of experience levels and tenures, and we’re building an environment that celebrates knowledge-sharing and mentorship. Our senior members enjoy one-on-one mentoring and thorough, but kind, code reviews. We care about your career growth and strive to assign projects that help our team members develop your engineering expertise so you feel empowered to take on more complex tasks in the future. jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, Leo Antenna Team
jobs.description: Amazon Leo is Amazon's low Earth orbit satellite network. Our mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will serve people and organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity. The Leo Antenna team is looking for a Software Development Engineer who is excited to work at the intersection of large-scale data systems, Amazon Web Services cloud services, data analysis, and radio frequency hardware. In this role, you will design and build Customer Terminal Fleet Health, the system that keeps a daily hardware health record for every customer terminal Leo operates and flags terminals whose hardware is starting to fail. You will turn telemetry from millions of satellite contacts a day into clear, trustworthy signals that tell engineers which terminals need attention and why. You do not need to come in as a radio frequency expert, but you should have a strong software engineering foundation, experience building data pipelines on Amazon Web Services, a high learning velocity, and the drive to understand phased array antennas, satellite links, and how hardware failures show up in telemetry. This is an individual contributor software development role for someone who enjoys ambiguous technical problems, can learn across disciplines, and wants to build data systems that directly improve the reliability of a satellite network. Export Control Requirement Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum. Key job responsibilities Design and build data pipelines on AWS (Step Functions, Athena, Glue, Iceberg, Lambda, S3) that process daily telemetry for the full fleet of customer terminals. Define and own the data model for fleet health: daily per-terminal aggregates, per-satellite views, and the history engineers use to investigate a single terminal. Partner with RF and antenna engineers to understand signal quality, temperature, reboot, and link metrics well enough to separate hardware failures from network, weather, and satellite effects. Develop and validate the rules and models that flag failing hardware, and measure how well they work against terminals returned for repair. Build infrastructure as code with AWS CDK, with deployment pipelines, monitoring, alarms, and integration tests that keep the system reliable. Build dashboards and tools that let engineering and operations teams explore fleet health, compare groups of terminals, and track the effect of software and hardware changes. Apply strong security and data-handling practices to sensitive customer and device data, including least-privilege access, encryption, and privacy controls. Collaborate with data platform and customer terminal software teams to onboard new data sources and improve the telemetry the system depends on. Write high-quality, maintainable code and documentation that other engineers and teams across Leo can build on. A day in the life You may start the day reviewing the overnight fleet health run, checking that every data source arrived and looking at which terminals were newly flagged. You might then sit down with antenna and radio frequency engineers on a group of terminals whose signal quality dropped, digging through the data together to decide whether it points to failing hardware, a software release, or something outside the terminal. Later, you may meet with the data platform and customer terminal software teams to onboard a new telemetry source, then write the infrastructure and pipeline code that brings it into the daily run with tests and alarms in place. You might finish the day with field operations, comparing the watch list against recent hardware returns to see which failures the system flagged early, which it missed, and what each returned terminal can teach the rules. Across all of it, your work helps engineers spot failing hardware before customers notice and measure the effect of software and hardware changes across the fleet. This role requires curiosity, technical depth, and the ability to move between data engineering, cloud infrastructure, and hardware context. You will not just write code; you will help define how Leo understands the health of every terminal in its fleet. About the team The Leo Customer Terminal Software Team supports the devices that connect customers to the Leo satellite network. We provide embedded application software and the underlying Linux system software for these terminals. We work hand in hand with hardware, product, and operations teams to deliver a great experience for our customers. As Leo moves toward full-scale production and global deployment, this is a compelling time to join and help shape how millions of people get online for the first time. - 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience - 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience - 1+ years of software development engineer or related occupational experience - 1+ years of designing and developing large-scale, multi-tiered, multi-threaded, embedded or distributed software applications, tools, systems, and services using: C#, C++, Java, or Perl experience - 1+ years of Object Oriented Design experience - Bachelor's degree or foreign equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field - Experience programming with at least one software programming language - 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience - Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status.
